chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about two men who have wealth between them, part of which is in their hands and part is absent from them. They divided the part that was in their hands, and each one of them managed his share of the absent part. One of them collected his share, while the other did not. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Whatever one of them collected, it is between them, according to what he spent to collect it.'

key_terms.غَائِبٌ: Absent (property or debt not currently in hand)

ai.seo_question: How is profit or debt divided between two business partners when one actively collects the debts and the other does not?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the distribution of profits in a partnership where one partner actively manages the 'absent' assets while the other remains passive. The ruling establishes that the active partner’s share of the collected wealth belongs jointly to both partners, with the active partner retaining only the specific costs or effort he expended in the collection process. This principle underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on equitable profit-sharing based on capital contribution rather than labor alone, unless explicitly agreed otherwise.
